concerns.text: The power analysis is described only as “compute MDES given the 6 h CPU budget and per‑chunk inference cost”. No expected effect size, variance estimate, or justification for the target N = 500 per language is provided. Without a concrete effect‑size assumption the sample size may be insufficient to detect realistic correlations, risking an under‑powered study.

Normalization is limited to dividing per‑token loss by the KenLM n‑gram probability. Token count is recorded as a confounder but never incorporated into the correlation analysis (e.g., as a covariate in a partial‑correlation or regression). This may leave residual frequency bias, threatening construct validity of the ‘loss’ measure.

The plan assumes code comments and documentation density are negligible. These factors can affect both complexity metrics (e.g., nesting depth) and LLM loss (comments are easy to predict). No strategy is described to quantify or control for comment density, which is a plausible confound.

Piecewise regression and change‑point detection are selected, but the model‑selection criterion is only “ΔAIC > 2”. Given multiple metrics and languages, this single threshold may lead to false‑positive non‑linear detections. A more robust approach (e.g., cross‑validation or bootstrap model‑selection) should be added to guard against over‑fitting.
